summary: Elmwood Home Care, a home healthcare provider serving Rhode Island and Massachusetts, disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to its systems between 2026-01-24 and 2026-02-13. Forensic investigation determined a threat group viewed or acquired patient files containing names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, other demographic data, medical information, and health insurance information. Lifepoint Health, Inc. disclosed that on Feb 22, 2026 an unauthorized third party used a compromised (stolen) user account to gain access to its internal environment and certain internal databases. The activity was detected the next day and contained within 24 hours. The exposed databases held names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and Social Security numbers of employees of contracted vendors (not patients or direct employees). Affected individuals were notified beginning April 23, 2026 and offered credit monitoring.

Clinical Registry Solutions (CRS), a Brooklyn, NY provider of clinical data abstraction and registry-support services to healthcare providers, suffered a cyberattack detected on April 9, 2026. An external actor gained unauthorized access to CRS's network and copied files containing protected health information belonging to patients of Dignity Health's St. Mary's Medical Center (names, medical record numbers, procedure dates) as well as CRS employee and company data. Mackay Sugar Limited, Australia's second-largest raw sugar producer, suffered a ransomware attack by The Gentlemen (Microsoft: Storm-2697) that surfaced on 2026-06-10 and forced two of its three Queensland mills (Farleigh and Racecourse) offline during the crushing season. The group named the company on its Tor-based leak site on 2026-06-15 with a countdown, claiming to have stolen corporate data (double-extortion), though no data had been published and the victim had not confirmed a data breach as of 2026-07-02.

Networking Technology Inc, doing business as RXNT — a cloud-based electronic prescribing, practice-management, and EHR SaaS vendor — suffered a hacking breach in which an external actor gained unauthorized access to its systems between March 1 and March 3, 2026 and obtained a copy of stored patient data belonging to many of its healthcare customers. Compromised data included names, dates of birth, contact information, patient IDs, prescription/medical information, and Social Security numbers, affecting tens of thousands of individuals across multiple states. Eastman Kodak Company confirmed a June 2026 data breach after the ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed on its dark-web leak site to have stolen over 2.2 million records of customer PII and internal corporate data, threatening to publish the data unless Kodak made contact by 18 June 2026. Kodak confirmed an unauthorized third party gained temporary access to a limited amount of its data, declined to pay, and engaged external cybersecurity experts and law enforcement.

Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) disclosed that attackers gained unauthorized access to internal IT systems and copied non-public data, including pseudonymized clinical-trial patient data (patient IDs, trial participation, sex, birth year, biomarkers, health/immunogenicity data, lifestyle factors), healthcare-provider contact details, internal AI model assets and other proprietary data.
